chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you have finished your Tawaf and reach the rear of the Ka'bah, which is opposite the Mustajar (the hanging curtain area) slightly before the Yemeni Corner, spread your hands upon the House, press your belly and cheek against the House, and say: "O Allah, the House is Your House, and the servant is Your servant, and this is the place of the one seeking refuge in You from the Fire." Then acknowledge to your Lord what you have done, for there is no believing servant who acknowledges to his Lord his sins in this place except that Allah will forgive him, if Allah wills." And whoever forgets the Iltezam, there is no need for him to repeat it. This was narrated.'

key_terms.الِالْتِزَامَ: Iltezam (pressing the chest/cheek against the Ka'bah)
key_terms.الْمُسْتَجَارِ: The Mustajar (the area behind the door of the Ka'bah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual of Iltezam in Tawaf and the supplication recited during it?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific location and method of *Iltezam* (pressing the body against the Ka'bah) at the spot opposite the *Mustajar* near the Yemeni Corner, a practice emphasized by the Imams as a locus for divine acceptance. It highlights the theological principle of *al-Qirar* (confession of sins) as a means to secure forgiveness, linking physical proximity to the House of God with spiritual humility and the hope for mercy.
